### Observed differences

- The execution order between two groups of activities reversed. In the earlier window, A26 ran before A35, A36 and A41 in about 98–99 in 100 traces, and A27 ran before them in about 99 in 100; in the later window, A35, A36 and A41 run before A26 in about 97–98 in 100 traces and before A27 in about 97 in 100. All six activities still occur together in every trace in both windows. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006]

- A26 and A27 now occur later within traces, and A35, A36 and A41 earlier: the mean relative position of A26 rose from about 0.53 to 0.62 and of A27 from about 0.38 to 0.47, while A35, A36 and A41 each fell from about 0.58 to about 0.42. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005]

- Successors were rewired around these groups. A25 led almost exclusively to A27 in the earlier window (about 97.5 in 100 outgoing transitions) and now splits roughly equally across A36, A41 and A35 (about 31–33 in 100 each). A26 previously led to A41, A35 and A36 (about 38, 33 and 28 in 100) and now leads almost exclusively to A30 (about 97.5 in 100). Each of A35, A36 and A41 sent about 28–34 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A30 before; now each sends about 31–33 in 100 to A27, and A30 is no longer a noticeable target. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- Step distances moved with the rewiring. A25 reached A27 immediately before (1 step in about 98 in 100 cases) and now reaches it only after 4–5 steps (about 90 in 100 at 4 steps); A26 reached A30 after 4–5 steps before and now reaches it immediately (1 step in about 98 in 100). The pairs A26→A35/A36/A41 and A35/A36/A41→A30, each observed in roughly 200 traces earlier, appear only 1–2 times later, while A25→A35 and A35→A27, almost unobserved earlier (1 trace each), now appear in about 199 of 200 traces. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the group of activities A35, A36 and A41, which previously executed after A26 and A27, now executes before them. In the earlier window the flow ran roughly A25 → A27 → {A35, A36, A41} → A30, with A26 also running before the group; in the later window A25 feeds into the group, the group runs ahead of both A26 and A27, the group exits to A27 instead of A30, and A26 proceeds directly to A30. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, LAG001, LAG003]

Supporting signs: the order reversal is near-complete on all six cross-group pairs while co-occurrence stays at 100 in 100, so participation and repetition are unchanged; the position shifts of all five activities point in the matching directions; the successor changes at A25, A26 and the group fit the new order; and 26 control-flow items qualified against about 0.6 expected if nothing had changed, far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]

Limitations: the DIR, POS, REL and LAG items largely reflect the same underlying traces, so their agreement is not independent confirmation. The evidence does not show the relative order of A26 versus A27 in either window, nor the internal sequence of A35, A36 and A41, and it cannot distinguish a relocation of the group within one flow from a change in the mix of two pre-existing orderings that would produce the same signals. Several LAG items rest on only 1–2 observations in one window. [LAG002, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009, LAG010]
